brief.headline: Fix the 40% return rate first, then push price toward ₹0.65–0.80 per cap using market data and three strong alternates.

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.65–0.80 per piece for 28 mm caps at our volume
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The market verdict says there's modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — that's our target band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: No change — hold at 30 days; focus energy on quality and price

brief.financialLeverage: Scorpion publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit, or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is very small, so we have little volume leverage. However, a 40% return rate screams serious quality or process problems — that's costly for them and us. The real leverage is that we have four solid alternates lined up (two listed firms, two private converters, all with pharma capability), plus six maker leads to qualify. They need to fix returns and meet market pricing, or we start qualifying a second source immediately.

evidence.point: Four out of ten items they deliver get sent back
Our annual spend with them is tiny
Market asking price for 28 mm caps runs ₹0.55–1.20 per piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95
Market verdict: modest room to drop to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec
HDPE resin import price stands at 87.61 ₹/kg as raw-material reference

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed, ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma — robust, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited — a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Manufacturer with pan-India reach; medium-confidence web lead for rigid plastic — needs audit and pricing.

risks: The 40% return rate is a red flag — until root cause (quality defect, wrong spec, paperwork) is nailed down and fixed, every order carries rework cost and line-stop risk for us.
Our ₹1.66 L spend gives us almost no volume muscle — they won't bend much on price for such a small account unless we credibly threaten to move the business.
No public financials means we're flying blind on their stability — if they're fragile and we squeeze too hard, they may just walk or fold.
We have six maker leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) but none are qualified yet — don't promise a switch until we've audited at least one and gotten a firm quote.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We need to talk about the 40% return rate and how we get your price in line with the ₹0.65–0.80 market band — we're qualifying alternates and can't carry this cost and disruption.
